summary: Independent CLI-only verification completed for the P1 desktop batch. Isley.dll compiled before the explicitly accepted Linux MSB3030 VoiceServer.exe copy failure. Existing pytest remained 17/17; the expanded 24-test suite is 23/24 because a new extracted-runtime pin-share edge test found that '__proto__' bypasses the claimed pinTypes whitelist. Normal pin export/import round-trip, malformed-input rejection, dedupe, clamping, 20-pin eviction, persistence/redraw gating, 111-command parity, marker interpolation contracts, below-35 vitals behavior, encounter history contracts, overlay lint, four Node suites, and six .NET verifiers passed. Windows WPF runtime flows were not executed on Linux.

minor.issue: The check !pinTypes[entry.t] is not an own-property whitelist. A valid share payload with t='__proto__' resolves Object.prototype, is imported as a saved pin, persisted, and drawn. This violates the requested pinTypes whitelist and permits malformed pin state. Reproduced against the extracted shipped functions in Node.

action_items: Enforce an own-property pin type check during share import, for example Object.hasOwn(pinTypes, entry.t), and preferably apply the same guard when restoring/exporting saved pins; rerun the 24-test pytest suite.
Run docs/WINDOWS_SMOKE_TEST.md on Windows to validate visual marker gliding/reduced motion and WPF clipboard/toast flows for pin sharing and encounter history.
critical_code_review_comments: Using plain object indexing as a whitelist accepts inherited names such as '__proto__', 'constructor', and 'toString'. Treat untrusted share-code type strings with Object.hasOwn or use a null-prototype map/Set.

context_for_next_testing_agent: CLI-only desktop repository; do not start web services or browser. The sole automated failure is test_pin_type_whitelist_rejects_inherited_object_keys. Existing 17 tests are green. The build's final MSB3030 for the absent Linux VoiceServer.exe apphost is accepted; the log confirms BurntHud emitted Isley.dll. Windows smoke behavior remains untested.
rca_of_the_issue: importPinShareCode evaluates pinTypes[entry.t] on a normal JavaScript object. Property lookup traverses Object.prototype, so '__proto__' is truthy even though it is not one of the seven pin type keys. Reproduction: encode [{t:'__proto__',x:10,y:20,l:'Prototype key'}] with the normal ISLEYPINS1 base64 format and call the extracted shipped import function; it returns 1 and appends the invalid pin. Use Object.hasOwn(pinTypes, entry.t) (and equivalent checks in storage restore/export) to close the prototype-chain bypass.
